articles.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.
articles.abstract: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events. This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed. Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment. In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk. Eli Lilly and Company.

articles.title: DNL343 and Disease Progression in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: DNL343 is a brain-penetrant small molecule that acts as an activator of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2b), designed to inhibit the integrated stress response. A prior phase 1B trial of DNL343 in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) provided evidence of a favorable safety profile, central nervous system penetrance, and target engagement based on integrated stress response biomarkers in blood and cerebrospinal fluid. To evaluate the safety and efficacy of a 200-mg formulation of DNL343 given once daily in individuals living with ALS. DNL343 was evaluated as a regimen of the HEALEY ALS Platform Trial, a double-blind, multiregimen, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at 74 centers in the US between May 24, 2023, and May 22, 2025. Eligible participants were randomized in a 3:1 ratio to receive DNL343 or matching placebo, with both groups enrolling concurrently. The analysis included shared randomized participants receiving placebo from an additional regimen. The study drug was administered for a placebo-controlled duration of 24 weeks. The primary analysis was a bayesian shared parameter model of function and survival that provided an integrated estimate of the relative rate of disease progression among participants receiving DNL343 relative to placebo. The model had components for function and survival linked through an integrated estimate of disease slowing in treatment relative to controls across the 2 outcomes (denoted as the disease rate ratio [DRR]). Several safety, secondary, and exploratory end points were also evaluated. A total of 259 screenings were completed in this regimen; 249 participants met eligibility and were randomized to DNL343 (n = 186) and regimen-specific placebo (n = 63), with an additional 76 participants from a concurrent regimen receiving placebo included for a total of 139 shared placebo participants (325 participants, with 196 (60.3%) male and mean [SD] age of 59.3 [11.5] years). The estimated median DRR common to the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised and survival was 1.04 (95% credible interval, 0.83-1.32; probability of DRR <1, 0.37). Secondary outcome measures were not statistically different between the DNL343 and placebo groups. Overall, the incidence rates of adverse events were similar in participants receiving DNL343 and placebo. In this randomized clinical trial, despite the relevance of the eIF2b activation pathway in ALS disease biology and supporting evidence of proof of mechanism and optimal dose selection in a prior phase 1B ALS clinical trial, 200-mg/d DNL343 did not show evidence of slowing disease progression in ALS, highlighting the need for alternative therapeutic approaches. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05842941.

articles.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
articles.abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. articles.abstract: Transcervical balloon catheters are used for cervical ripening in patients undergoing trial of labor after cesarean delivery, but their association with uterine rupture risk remains uncertain, particularly across different induction comparators. To estimate comparator-specific associations between transcervical balloon cervical ripening and complete uterine rupture during trial of labor after cesarean. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies identified through PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online, Embase, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from inception through June 2026, without language restrictions, supplemented by reference lists and trial registries (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; registration number CRD420261444368).Eligible studies evaluated Foley, single-balloon, or double-balloon catheters for cervical ripening after a previous low-transverse cesarean delivery. Comparative observational studies involving spontaneous labor, oxytocin, or prostaglandins were included in quantitative synthesis. Amniotomy alone was a prespecified eligible comparator, but no study reported a separable amniotomy-only arm. Single-arm cohorts were summarized descriptively, and randomized trials were synthesized qualitatively. Primary analyses were restricted to studies reporting complete uterine rupture separately. Because catheter placement was generally followed by amniotomy, oxytocin, or both, the exposure was classified as a balloon-based induction strategy rather than catheter use in isolation. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tool, the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Comparator-specific odds ratios and absolute risk differences were estimated using Mantel-Haenszel methods, with Peto and DerSimonian-Laird models used in sensitivity analyses. Potentially overlapping Swedish cohorts were not pooled. Eighteen nonrandomized studies and two randomized trials contributed 28,035 study observations, including 5,516 balloon exposures. Compared with prostaglandin induction, balloon-based induction was associated with lower odds of complete uterine rupture across three cohorts (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio, 0.43; 95% confidence interval, 0.26-0.72), with an absolute risk difference of -19 per 1,000 (95% confidence interval, -31 to -7) across four cohorts. A potentially overlapping Swedish cohort and a cohort reporting a combined rupture/dehiscence endpoint yielded concordant estimates, while 1 randomized trial reported no ruptures. No statistically significant difference was detected compared with oxytocin alone (odds ratio, 0.24; 95% confidence interval, 0.05-1.18) or spontaneous labor (seven cohorts; odds ratio, 1.29; 95% confidence interval, 0.90-1.84). Exclusion of the most influential spontaneous-labor cohort yielded an odds ratio of 1.09 (95% confidence interval, 0.73-1.62). Across all pharmacologic comparators, the pooled odds ratio was 0.40 (95% confidence interval, 0.25-0.66). Uterine dehiscence was reported more frequently following balloon-based induction (five studies; odds ratio, 1.86; 95% confidence interval, 1.06-3.29), with directionally concordant estimates compared with oxytocin-based induction (odds ratio, 1.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.83-3.92), spontaneous labor (odds ratio, 2.24; 95% confidence interval, 0.91-5.52), and prostaglandins (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 0.15-7.84; P=.80 for subgroup difference). Mechanical cervical ripening remains a reasonable option for carefully selected candidates requiring induction, provided that appropriate counseling, continuous monitoring, and immediate access to emergency cesarean delivery are available.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' interventions on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients.
articles.abstract: Vascular surgeons are treating more older, frail and multimorbid patients. Integrated care models including both surgeons and geriatricians have improved peri-operative outcomes in orthopaedics. This meta-analysis investigated the impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' services on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients. PubMed, Scopus, Embase and recent conference abstracts were searched for studies of all methodologies comparing outcomes before and after the introduction of 'Vascular Geriatrics' service. Risk of bias was assessed using Methodological Index for Non-Randomised Studies criteria for non-randomised studies and Risk of Bias Tool (Version Two) tool for randomised. Certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations analysis. Meta-analyses compared the relative risks of inpatient mortality, complications, discharge to home and 30-day readmission using a random-effects model. Length of stay (LOS) in days was compared using mean difference. Eight studies with 2441 patients were included. Models included outpatient pre-operative comprehensive geriatric assessment, inpatient geriatric liaison service and geriatrician-surgeon co-management. 'Vascular Geriatrics' was associated with a lower risk of inpatient mortality (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.9, P = .010), cardiac complications (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.19-0.62, P < .001) and infective complications (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38-0.63, P < .001). Delirium risk was reduced but not significantly (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.25-1.34, P = .20). There was no association in LOS (P = .37), discharge to home (P = .55) or 30-day readmission risk (P = .64). Though study quality was poor, formalised geriatric involvement was associated with a decreased risk of adverse peri-operative outcomes in vascular patients compared to traditional care models. Further studies are needed to investigate the most effective design of geriatrician-surgeon partnership.

articles.title: Interventions to Support Parents Whose Babies Cry Excessively: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Parents report that around 10% to 20% of babies cry a lot without an apparent reason during early infancy. This "excessive" infant crying can lead to adverse outcomes, including parental depression, breastfeeding cessation, impaired parent-child relationships, and, in extreme cases, infant abuse. Cost-effective parent-support services are needed. To assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of interventions designed to support parents of excessively crying babies. MEDLINE, Embase, EconLit, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, CINAHL and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 8th April 2025. The NIHR CRN database and handsearching were used to identify further studies. Comparative studies reporting parental outcomes for any intervention supporting parents of excessively crying infants aged ≤1 year were included. Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed when possible; otherwise, narrative synthesis was conducted. Meta-analysis found that educational interventions significantly reduced parental stress or anxiety. Narrative analyses produced mixed findings, but components common to successful educational interventions were indicated. Meta-analyses of studies administering probiotics to infants found significant improvements in parents' quality of life but not in parental depression. No safety data and limited economic evidence were found. Few studies measured similar enough parental outcomes to be pooled in meta-analysis. Risk of bias ranged from unclear to high risk. Educational and probiotic interventions show promise for supporting parents of excessively crying babies. Additional controlled trials employing evidence-based interventions and outcome measures and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to build on these findings.

articles.title: International recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica.
articles.abstract: The study aims to develop international recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). An international, multidisciplinary task force of 30 members from 12 countries was convened; the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standard operating procedures were followed. Six clinical key questions addressing the role of imaging (ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) in diagnosis, monitoring, outcome prediction, and technical aspects in PMR were the basis for a systematic literature review. Recommendations were formulated based on evidence and expert opinion and refined iteratively until consensus was achieved. The level of agreement was assessed by voting. Three overarching principles and 7 recommendations were developed. PMR remains primarily a clinical diagnosis. Imaging is neither required to confirm PMR in patients with a high clinical probability of the disease nor to exclude PMR in case of low clinical probability. Imaging is most useful in patients with intermediate pretest probability (ie, atypical presentations or suspected alternative/overlapping conditions). No single imaging modality demonstrated sufficient accuracy to be recommended as a first-line test; therefore, imaging should be individualised according to clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, access, and local expertise. Vascular imaging should be performed when overlap with giant cell arteritis is suspected, whereas systematic screening for subclinical vasculitis is not supported by current evidence. Utilising imaging for disease monitoring or outcome prediction is currently not recommended. These recommendations provide the first evidence-based guidance for the use of imaging in PMR, reinforcing clinical assessment as the cornerstone of diagnosis and positioning imaging as a context-driven adjunct.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To compare the effects of aerobic exercise, resistance exercise, and combined interventions on pain, function, and quality of life (QoL) in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA) at the short term (≤12 weeks) and long term (>12 weeks).  Intervention systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA).  MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL, PEDro, AMED, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception until July 2025.  We included randomized controlled trials of patients with knee OA that evaluated exercise interventions aimed at improving pain, function, and QoL.  Using random-effects models, the NMA synthesized effect sizes and ranked interventions by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), with evidence certainty assessed via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.  Thirty-five trials (n = 3808 patients) were included. For pain, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect among the interventions (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.937, low certainty). For function, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect estimates (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), followed by long-term aerobic exercise (SMD = -0.540, very low certainty). Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) for improving QoL.  Aerobic and resistance exercise, alone or in combination, and delivered over the short- or long-term, improved pain, function, and QoL for patients with knee OA. Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had clinically meaningful improvements for pain, with relatively favorable effects on function and QoL. Evidence regarding the clinical significance of long-term exercise interventions was limited. .

articles.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; =0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47];  < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.
